problem: Training-free VLM ObjectNav agents reset all scene knowledge after each episode, so in recurring deployment (same home/office) discovered room connectivity, object viewpoints and successful approaches are wasted. Existing memory methods only serve the current episode, and persistent-navigation work (GOAT-Bench, SSMG-Nav) assumes continuous goal sequences with physical state continuity.
motivation: A service robot repeatedly visiting the same scene should reuse experience without retraining, oracle maps or room labels. Cross-episode reuse removes physical-state continuity, so memory must support re-localization after independent initialization and target-conditioned retrieval.
key_idea: Keep a persistent scene-scoped hierarchical visual-topological memory (a coarse room graph indexing room-owned visual object records, with in-room vs remote-visible evidence and success-backed approaches) and use it to re-localize, retrieve and softly guide a frozen VLM ObjectNav agent in later independently initialized episodes.
insight: Every component matters on HM3D v0.1 (ablation): removing topology drops SR from 59.6 to 56.5, visual evidence to 57.7, the guard to 58.0. Notably, the no-persistence variant reaches 59.4 SR but SPL falls to 30.5 versus 31.8, so persistence mainly buys path efficiency, while its SR value is small. Structured room-owned visual memory beats free-form textual memory (WMNav+TM is only 56.5 SR on v0.1 and 66.5 on v0.2). The gains are modest, and the bootstrap CI for SR over the reset control includes zero on v0.2.
method: Semantic evidence: Qwen3-VL-Plus reads the egocentric RGB each step and returns room label, visible objects and a scene summary; these are cleaned (negations and room words removed) and objects seen through openings are marked remote-visible.

Hierarchical memory: a room-topology graph (room nodes with aliases, confidence, visit stats; edges are observed transitions), where each room owns in-room and remote-visible object nodes (confidence, count, viewpoints, summaries, hints, success-backed approaches).

Room localization: an unweighted sum of semantic (name, object-overlap Jaccard, summary-keyword Jaccard), topological (same or adjacent to the previous room) and spatial (distance to stored positions) scores; the argmax room is assigned, and new rooms are promoted only after repeated tentative support or a high-confidence observation.

Memory update: object-node association by category and description compatibility; confidence increments; success-backed increment after successful episodes; edges added on confirmed transitions; memory is written after each episode and persists per scene.

Hierarchical retrieval: rank rooms by confidence + observation count + success count with in-room evidence preferred over remote-visible; BFS gives the room-hop path from the current room to the target-bearing room; the resulting prior contains evidence type, room, confidence, viewpoint and path.

Observation-grounded guidance: the prior is added to the VLM prompt as soft context and can override the VLM choice only via a lexical-agreement score B over current navigable candidates, if B exceeds a threshold.
Conservative execution guard: handles blocked motion, no progress, revisits, oscillation and premature stopping; inactive by default and always preserves stop when the target is visible.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-Plus (frozen) on top of the WMNav pipeline
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 640x480, 79° HFOV, 14° downward pitch, plus estimated pose
setting.action_space: depth-based navigable candidates (polar displacement + text description) chosen by the VLM, plus stop; WMNav controller
setting.privileged: none (memory built only from self-acquired observations; no GT object locations, semantic maps or room labels); episodes run consecutively per scene with memory persisting

numbers.eval_set_note: HM3D v0.1, 2,000 episodes over 20 scenes; scenes run sequentially with persistent memory
numbers.extra: cross-episode memory persistence within scene; 40-step budget

numbers_note: Only SR/SPL reported. The paper says 'validation splits' and I labeled them 'val' (not val-unseen). HM3D v0.2 is listed as other: since the canonical list has no v0.2 entry.
results: Under matched 40-step comparisons, VTM-Nav reaches 59.6/72.0/44.3 SR on HM3D v0.1/v0.2/MP3D, beating the memory-reset WMNav control (55.0/70.0/43.5) by 4.6/2.0/0.8 SR with comparable or higher SPL. It also beats WMNav with textual memory by 3.1 and 5.5 SR on the two HM3D sets. The early-to-late progression on v0.2 is +2.7 SR for VTM-Nav vs +0.7 for the reset control.
limitations: Gains are modest and partly not statistically resolved (HM3D v0.2 SR CI vs the reset control is [-0.60,3.87]); the MP3D gain is only 0.8 SR, and the progression analysis is descriptive, since episode order and difficulty are uncontrolled.

Compared only against WMNav variants under a 40-step budget with a Qwen3-VL-Plus backbone; published baselines are not directly comparable. The lexical re-ranking is coupled with memory retrieval, and the guard cannot be cleanly isolated.
Depends on VLM room/object labels and hand-set thresholds and lexical dictionaries; the assumption of many consecutive episodes in the same scene may not hold in deployment.
